findings.location: items/thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral.md, ## Statement, lines 34–36; the Given clause at line 40 also omits the measure-space data.
findings.evidence: The statement introduces only a nonnegative measurable sequence and its pointwise limit, then uses integrals with respect to μ without specifying a domain, sigma-algebra, or measure space. The Given clause likewise does not supply these data. The assigned consumer invokes this theorem in steps 2.1 and 4.1 for integrals with respect to P. The dependency needs an explicit measure-space hypothesis (X, A, μ), with all functions measurable on that space. Hunter, Measure Theory, §4.2, Theorem 4.6 (with the measure-space setting in Proposition 4.5), states monotone convergence for functions on a measure space.
